This reduces both binary size and startup time significantly."},{"kind":"paragraph","text":"The proposal introduces struct and array types, along with typed references. Compilers can now emit allocations that the host runtime understands, and the runtime can collect them without scanning a black-box heap, which is a substantial change."},{"kind":"heading","level":2,"text":"Why it matters for edge computing"},{"kind":"paragraph","text":"Edge workers care about cold start latency above everything else. A smaller module with fewer runtime dependencies starts faster, and that is exactly what the GC proposal enables for compiled languages targeting the web platform today."},{"kind":"list_item","text":"Smaller binaries"},{"kind":"list_item","text":"Faster cold starts"},{"kind":"list_item","text":"Better interoperability with JavaScript objects"},{"kind":"paragraph","text":"Comment one Comment one Comment one"},{"kind":"paragraph","text":"Comment two Comment two Comment two"}],"text":"Understanding WASM GC\n\nWASM GC gives WebAssembly a native reference type system, so languages with managed memory no longer need to ship their own garbage collector inside the linear memory. This reduces both binary size and startup time significantly.\n\nThe proposal introduces struct and array types, along with typed references. Compilers can now emit allocations that the host runtime understands, and the runtime can collect them without scanning a black-box heap, which is a substantial change.\n\nWhy it matters for edge computing\n\nEdge workers care about cold start latency above everything else. A smaller module with fewer runtime dependencies starts faster, and that is exactly what the GC proposal enables for compiled languages targeting the web platform today.\n\nSmaller binaries\n\nFaster cold starts\n\nBetter interoperability with JavaScript objects\n\nComment one Comment one Comment one\n\nComment two Comment two Comment two","markdown":"# Understanding WASM GC\n\nWASM GC gives WebAssembly a native reference type system, so languages with managed memory no longer need to ship their own garbage collector inside the linear memory. This reduces both binary size and startup time significantly.\n\nThe proposal introduces struct and array types, along with typed references. Compilers can now emit allocations that the host runtime understands, and the runtime can collect them without scanning a black-box heap, which is a substantial change.\n\n## Why it matters for edge computing\n\nEdge workers care about cold start latency above everything else. A smaller module with fewer runtime dependencies starts faster, and that is exactly what the GC proposal enables for compiled languages targeting the web platform today.\n\n- Smaller binaries\n\n- Faster cold starts\n\n- Better interoperability with JavaScript objects\n\nComment one Comment one Comment one\n\nComment two Comment two Comment two","metadata":{"site_name":null,"description":"A short introduction to WASM GC.","lead_image":null,"lang":"en","published_at":null,"keywords":[],"jsonld":null},"score":11.0000,"rules_version":"1.0.0"}
